title: CombatState (GameObservation.State)
description: Shape of the 'state' dict inside GameObservation (Sts2Emulator.Dto.GameObservation.State), as built by GameInstance.BuildFullStateDict() - the authoritative, no-normalization state surface for RL. Combat-only fields (hand/drawPile/.../enemies) are present only while a combat is in progress (_combatState != null); map-only fields (currentActIndex/actFloor/.../map) are present only when a run/map exists (HasMap). A pure combat-scenario reset via ResetFromScenario has no map, so only the base + combat fields appear. Source of truth: GameInstance.cs BuildFullStateDict/BuildCardListDict/BuildRelicsDict/BuildPotionsDict/BuildPowersDict/BuildEnemiesDict/BuildIntentDict/BuildMapDict - re-derive this schema from there if the emulator changes.

stepIndex.description: Monotonically increasing count of Step() calls processed by this GameInstance since Reset/ResetFromScenario.

stars.description: Regent-flavored combat resource exposed by GameInstance.BuildFullStateDict(). Present during combat; null outside combat or if no PlayerCombatState exists.

potions.description: One entry per potion slot; null means that slot is empty.

deck.description: The player's full deck (all piles combined at the model level, i.e. the persistent deck list, not any one pile).

drawPile.description: combat-only. Index 0 is top-of-pile / next drawn.

pendingChoice.description: combat-only, present when the engine is waiting for a mid-effect card choice (e.g. WISH draw-to-hand, transform, discard, upgrade). The options list is ordered and corresponds 1:1 to currently offered choice_card legal actions.

map.description: map-only, see BuildMapDict: columns, rows, points[] ({col,row,pointType,children[]}), startingPoint, bossPoint, secondBossPoint, visited[], currentCoord.

id.description: raw entry id, matches Common/ids/cards.json keys after normalization

cost.description: with cost modifiers applied, floored at 0

tinkerTimeType.description: MAD_SCIENCE-specific per-instance state exported by recent Emulator builds; required for exact scenario reconstruction once the card has taken on a concrete embedded effect.

tinkerTimeRider.description: MAD_SCIENCE-specific rider metadata paired with tinkerTimeType when present.

id.description: every power id ends in '_POWER', e.g. 'STRENGTH_POWER'

index.description: Position within CombatState.Enemies at observation time - disambiguates duplicate monster types (e.g. two 'FLYCONID') within ONE decision, and matches Parameters.enemyIndex on a 'choice_target' LegalAction (see legal_action_schema.json) taken from the SAME state. CAVEAT (verified against engine source, contradicts GameInstance.cs's own doc comment on this field): this index is NOT stable across a death. CombatState.cs physically removes a dead creature from the underlying list (`_enemies.Remove(creature)`, not merely isAlive=false), so every enemy after it recompacts down by one position immediately - confirmed to happen even within a single Step() call, not only across separate emulator restores (see STS2_RL/Combat/tests/test_scenario_v2.py::test_target_tracking_after_death). Use 'index' to resolve a target choice within one get_legal_actions()->step() round trip; do NOT cache an index value across multiple steps once any enemy may have died since - re-resolve from the latest observation every time. DO NOT use 'name' (empty string under headless TestMode - confirmed) or 'id' (shared by every instance of the same monster type) or a 'choice_target' action's own ActionId (indexes only the currently-alive candidate list, which also shifts) as a substitute - 'index' is still the best available disambiguator for a single decision, just not a cross-turn tracking key.

id.description: monster entry id, or LogName fallback for id-less mock/scenario enemies. Shared by every instance of the same monster type - use 'index' (not this) to address a specific enemy. Use this (not 'name') for human-readable display/logging.

name.description: LogName - empty string in this headless harness (TestMode's headless localization produces no display text). Not useful for display; definitely not usable as a stable identifier.

maxHp.description: CAVEAT: EnemyScenario has no MaxHp input field - after ResetFromScenario, every restore treats the scenario's Hp as 100%, so this value 'chases' current hp down on repeated restores unless the caller patches it back (battle_emulator.py's BattleEmulator._wrap does this in Python - see its module comment).

attackDamage.description: present only for Attack-shaped intents where the damage hook succeeded

stateLog.description: move-state history, oldest first - required input for scenarios reproducing a monster mid-pattern (see EnemyScenario.StateLog)

scenarioRestorable.description: True only for StartOfCombat choices that may be round-tripped through CombatScenario.PendingChoice.
